motivation: Phase 15 showed that the frozen symmetric 16-feature hypothesis class is a real limitation for directional advection. Phase 16 tests whether a generic differential-operator basis, rather than an advection-specific branch or law label, can recover advection while retaining the previously confirmed wave, Gray-Scott, and unseen NLS behavior.

frozen_representation.state_representation: same Phase-10/14 18-bit causal companded innovation representation

operator_definitions.Lap: same periodic 5-point Laplacian used in prior phases

primary_gate: PASS only if all 15 primary companded rollout ratios are < 1.0 versus raw-state persistence in every one of the 3 fresh registered replicates (45/45 cells). No failed or consumed replicate may be retried or replaced.
secondary_diagnostics: raw-state rollout using the same 18-feature library
raw-state rollout using the old frozen 16-feature library
failure_policy: Any registered primary cell >= 1.0 makes Phase 16 FAIL. Keep unfavorable results. Infrastructure-incomplete runs are neither PASS nor FAIL and their consumed seeds are not reused.
claim_limit: A PASS would show that one generic hand-designed differential operator library can cover these four synthetic PDE families under the tested regimes. It would not establish unrestricted law discovery or novel physics.
